Each meal costs $8 to make, and the owner prices it using cost-plus pricing with a 25% mark-up, giving a selling price of $10. The owner employs a part-time assistant at $12 an hour to cope with the lunch rush of 240 meals between 12:00 and 14:00. The decision will be reviewed at the end of September, after 8 weeks of trading data.

scenario_stem:
Cindervale Ceramic Company, a private limited company founded by Priya Anand, has developed a premium artisan pizza oven for back gardens. Production cost is $380 per unit. Development took 4 years and cost $260,000. Founder Priya Anand must choose a launch price for next spring: a price skimming start at $950 targeting enthusiasts, or a penetration start at $520, below the market leader's comparable oven at $640.

Forecasts suggest 900 units in year 1 at $950, or 1,700 units at $520. Skimming would earn a $570 margin per oven; penetration only $140 per oven, worth $238,000 across 1,700 units. Annual capacity is 1,800 units. Priya is keen to recover the development spend quickly, while sales director Marco Diaz argues share must come before profit. The board meets in 2 weeks to decide.

scenario_stem:
Saltmarsh Cove Hotel, a 120-room coastal resort owned by a public limited company, struggles with off-season occupancy of only 38% in January and February. Room price is the single biggest factor in guests' booking decisions, according to its own survey of 1,400 past guests. The sales director proposes two routes to lift the off-season: promotional pricing — 25% off, rooms from $160 down to $120 for 6 weeks — or dynamic pricing — weekends at $260, midweeks at $130, day-before rates from $90 — all off-season.

Last year's January–February revenue was $640,000, and the forecast is 55% occupancy with promotional pricing versus 60% with dynamic pricing. Part-time hours would rise by 480 hours a month under dynamic pricing if occupancy reaches 60%. The hotel employs 46 full-time staff and 30 part-time. The board meets on 10 December to choose.
